findings.text: CPU hotplug and early initialization surface includes a reconciler callable from CPU hotplug context, an SMP seeder for top effective sets plus node subscription and migration workqueue setup, and a current-task memory allowance initializer.
CPU allowance surface provides locked and self-locking mask calculators plus a version-gated forced fallback helper reporting whether it installed the cset mask, and a CPU count query.

Memory-node surface exposes per-task mask retrieval, intersection validity against current allowance, single-node permission evaluation, cgroup effective-node copying, spread-rotor advancement with lazy seeding, pairwise task overlap testing, and log plus sequence-file emitters.

Debug controller surface offers early enablement for default-hierarchy inspection with implicit presence and threaded support; device-memory surface offers minimum and low-water setters forwarding to per-pool accounting.
Hotplug reconciler is entered while CPU hotplug protection is already held and performs top-level resynchronization, descendant propagation and deferred scheduling maintenance before returning.
Node-state change callback unconditionally runs full reconciliation and signals successful handling.
Early SMP entry seeds top effective state from live system masks, preserves the initial memory allowance, subscribes to node changes and establishes the ordered migration workqueue.
Early current-task memory entry grants allowance on every node.
Early debug activation entry publishes default-hierarchy inspection files and enables implicit plus threaded controller behavior.

Top effective CPU and memory-node sets track system active availability; version one also mirrors availability into allowed sets while version two leaves allowed sets alone; CPUs reserved for subpartitions are removed from top effective, with total overlap clearing the reservation.

Temporary mask storage for descendant updates is requested only in version two mode and allocation failure degrades to a null helper pointer passed through to per-descendant handling rather than aborting reconciliation; storage is released at end.

Task CPU allowance computation distinguishes top membership: non-top tasks start from their cset guarantee while top members and empty results fall back to task-possible CPUs minus partition reservations, widening to all possible CPUs when no online overlap remains.
Fallback allowance in version two mode applies the task cset mask through forced assignment only when that mask is contained in task-possible CPUs, returning whether an update occurred.
CPU count query returns online population by default and, in version two mode only, returns the weight of the effective CPU set of the cgroup effective state when present.
Task memory-node allowance query derives an online-guaranteed mask from the task cset and returns it by value.
Node-mask validity check reports whether the supplied mask intersects the current task memory allowance.

Node allocation permission grants interrupt context, already-allowed nodes, OOM victims, exiting tasks and all version two callers without further checks; hardwall-flagged requests outside allowance are denied, while other version one requests outside allowance are decided by membership in the nearest ancestor with exclusive or hardwall property.

Cgroup memory-node query returns full memory availability when no cgroup is supplied, when not in version two mode, or when no effective state exists; otherwise it copies the effective memory set of the looked-up cgroup state.

Memory spreading advances a supplied rotor to the next node contained in current task allowance, with the task-level helper lazily seeding an uninitialized rotor from a random allowed node before advancing.
Pairwise task comparison reports whether the two tasks memory allowances overlap.
Diagnostic emitters expose task memory allowance: one appends cset name and bitmask forms to the active log line, the other formats fixed allowance and list lines into sequence output.
Debug subsystem state allocation creates a zeroed generic state object and reports out-of-memory on failure; release frees the container.
Debug numeric readers expose per-cgroup task population and a releasable predicate true only when the cgroup has no populated tasks and no online child states.

Current set diagnostics report the current set pointer with reference versus task counts, enumerate attached subsystem states per registered subsystem, expose the reference count alone, and list hierarchy roots with group names using a bounded temporary name buffer.

Per-cgroup linkage dump walks all sets attached to the cgroup, showing domain versus threaded relationships, reference surplus beyond task count with init-set adjustment, up to a bounded number of member task identifiers plus overflow count, dead marking, and summary tallies.

Subsystem-state dump lists each bound subsystem identifier, name, state pointer, numeric identity, online count and parent identity for a live cgroup; mask dump renders subtree control and subtree state masks as ordered subsystem-name lists.

Helpers convert generic subsystem state to device-memory cgroup state by container offset, fetch the current task state through its device-memory association, and map a state to its parent or null at the root.
Resource limit setters forward the supplied value to the pool usage-counter minimum and low-water interfaces respectively, ignoring blocking hints.

Hotplug reconciliation requires CPU hotplug protection on entry, serializes assessment under the global cpuset mutex, mutates top effective and allowed fields only under interrupt-disabled callback spin protection, and walks descendants under RCU with per-descendant online reference held across task updates.

One CPU-allowance accessor requires the caller already hold callback protection and asserts it, while the companion accessor internally acquires and releases interrupt-disabled callback protection around the same computation.

Task memory-mask retrieval and version one ancestor permission evaluation hold interrupt-disabled callback protection while inspecting cset masks; pairwise and current-mask intersection checks need no locks.

Debug sequence readers that walk set or cgroup linkage require live-knob validation where they resolve the target and hold interrupt-disabled set spin protection across list and reference-count inspection; the solitary reference-count numeric reader uses RCU alone.

Device-memory region and pool list synchronization is serialized by a single global spinlock; region list membership additionally tolerates RCU lookup while pool list mutation relies on the spinlock only.

Debug exposes parallel legacy and default file tables sharing taskcount and current-set files restricted to root where appropriate, differing only in naming of linkage, state and mask files and terminated by an empty entry; the subsystem descriptor wires generic alloc and free handlers with legacy files always present.

Device-memory region descriptor holds a lifetime reference count, RCU free head, global region linkage, pool list, byte size, driver-supplied name, unregistered flag forbidding new pools and reclaim, optional driver operations and reclaim private data.

Per-cgroup device-memory state embeds the generic subsystem state and owns a pool list; per-pool state links its region and owning cgroup state, carries RCU-protected set linkage and unprotected region linkage, RCU head, usage counter, parent pool pointer, reference count and initialization flag.

After descendant propagation the hotplug path conditionally refreshes scheduling domains when a force flag is set and conditionally queues a static delayed housekeeping work item when an invalidation flag is set, tolerating requeue before prior work execution because the worker ignores its container.

Pool lifetime uses reference counting with unconditional acquire, zero-aware conditional acquire, and release that defers destruction through RCU when the last reference drops; RCU destruction drops the parent reference and region reference before freeing, while explicit pool removal unlinks region membership before dropping a reference.
Cgroup effective memory copy is performed without cpuset or callback locks and may race with allowance rebinds, yielding stale node constraints by design.

Forced fallback samples cset state without locks and may install a transient mask; correctness depends on a concurrent attach or mask update repairing the task mask under request locking plus later runqueue selection.
Tasks in the top cset receive no mask update during hotplug reconciliation, so allowance calculation must compensate by including offline CPUs for top members and empty results.
Maximum device-memory reclaim retry bound is sixteen.
Per set diagnostic task display bound is twenty five entries before overflow summarization.
